messages.text: Apple Music Rebrands With a Look Made by Sound. Created with TBWA\Media Arts Lab and Fred Again, Apple Music's new identity is built on ripples of sound.
Kohl’s Brings Back Ellie Kemper for Holiday Ad Campaign. The retail chain is taking shoppers to "The North Kohl's."
The Best CMOs Don’t Just Run Marketing ft. Kellyn Smith Kenny of AT&T. Plus, why great marketing leaders need courage and patience.

Purpose Over Product: The Brand-Building Playbook of Paulie Dery and Victoria Lozano. The CMOs of AG1 and Crayola on building authentic communities, embedding products into existing routines, and reframing competition.
PepsiCo and AB InBev Vet Takes CMO Post at Troubled Diageo North America. Sebnem Erim joins as the North American division turned in the spirits giant's weakest results in 2026
ADWEEK’s TVNewser Introduces the New and Improved Daily Cable News Ratings. TVNewser’s daily ratings posts return in a new and interactive format.
Walmart Embraces AI Agents That Shop on Behalf of Customers. The retailer is setting the rules AI shopping agents will have to follow.
Meta Beats Q3 Expectations With Strong Earnings. The company says its AI investments are already paying off for advertisers

Tilly Norwood Tells All. This story was originally published in On Background with Mark Stenberg, a free, weekly newsletter that explores the key themes shaping the media industry. You can sign up for it here. […]

Marcel Gets its First CEO as Publicis Competes With Off-the-Shelf AI. Scott Hagedorn and Sam Levine Archer named CEO and CSO of the holdco’s AI platform, which started life as an employee tool and now builds agents for more than 90 clients.

Rosenberg: Russia agrees to Ukraine talks but sees little to talk about in new peace push. President Vladimir Putin does not feel under pressure right now to end the war, the BBC's Russia Editor writes.
Airbnb hosts can no longer make guests strip beds and wash dishes under new rules. The updated policy will apply to all reservations booked on the accommodation site on or after 20 November.
Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds. A new study finds Rosalind Franklin is the only woman named in Key Stage 4 science specifications.

Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma. Women are sharing their experiences with chronic urinary tract infections on social media in an effort to break the stigma surrounding UTIs.
Better weather, pay, more opportunities: Why graduates are ditching the UK to move abroad. With graduate jobs hard to come by, more young adults are reported to be considering emigrating.
The real reasons there are so few young politicians in the US. No country for young men and women: why do older politicians seem to have such a tight grip on the US political system?
Smith & Head out as South Africa close on win over Australia - scorecard. Latest scorecard from the second Test between South Africa and Australia in Gqeberha.
Vickery's journey from World Cup winner to bodybuilder at 50. Why England Rugby World Cup winner Phil Vickery has started entering bodybuilding competitions at the age of 50.

How Arab parties could hold critical balance of power in Israeli election. Disaffection has often driven down turnout among Arab Israelis, but there is a strong push to get rid of the right-wing governing coalition.
Is the UK set to green-light a huge untapped oil field in the North Atlantic?. Scotland editor James Cook visits Rosebank - the UK's largest known untapped oilfield - in the North Atlantic.
Dame Judi Dench: 'I can't do a play, a film or read any more'. The actress tells BBC Radio 4's Today programme about how her eye condition has affected her life.
Some New Yorkers back ban on horse-drawn carriages, but drivers fear for incomes. As councillors prepare to banish the vehicles, views in Central Park are divided over the 160-year-old tradition.
Tougher punishments for criminals who refuse to attend sentencing backed by victim's family. The aunt of Zara Aleena says the new powers for judges will "rebalance the power" from offender to victim.
MI5 spied on NHS founder Nye Bevan for more than 20 years, newly released files show. He came to its attention in the 1930s when he was considered a left-wing firebrand.
Barclays cutting 5,000 jobs as it increases reliance on AI. The bank says it is using more AI leading to a 5% reduction in its workforce.
Police investigate Married at First Sight Australia after 'inappropriate' allegations. New South Wales Police say inquiries took place "following a report of inappropriate content being shared".
Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb. It has been a dramatic, public and global response, but the cyber event hasn't happened yet.
Legendary video game studio BioWare closes after 31 years. The influential studio that made Mass Effect and Dragon Age announces it is closing its doors.
Two storms in two days as Austen and Boelo head for UK. The Met Office has named a new storm, Boelo, which is set to bring another round of stormy weather to the UK over the weekend.
Retired decorator's Pokémon cards sell for £1.5m after years in attic. He says he found treasure in his attic where the collection had been stored for 15 years.

'Not what a captain should be' - the debate around Fernandes' outburst. Bruno Fernandes' comments after Manchester United's humbling by Como have got fans and pundits talking - but what now for the captain?
Russell Brand accuser said alleged rape 'really hurt', court hears. The friend of a woman claiming to have been raped by Russell Brand says she said he was "quite aggressive".

'Ten years of hate and abuse' - Schoeman on viral victory over Brownlees. Henri Schoeman, who took a viral 2016 Triathlon World Series Grand Final over Jonny Brownlee, reveals the decade of abuse in the race's aftermath.
First human case of Shamonda virus detected in France, officials say. The disease, which usually affects cattle, has been identified in a patient who died in early October.
Moment man rescued from sinking car by Australian TV reporter. Journalist Will Murray describes how he and a bystander saved an SUV driver from his vehicle.
Tour de France UK stages in detail - where can you watch?. The full route for the 2027 Tour de France is announced in Paris, with street-by-street details of the six stages in the UK revealed.
What is PHP and why did it spark an international cyber-security alert?. AI uncovered long-hidden programming flaws, triggering a rare global cyber-security response.
At least four dead after storm brings flooding to southern France. The deaths include two women found drowned in a cellar in the Bouches-du-Rhône region.
Katie Price's ex not guilty of raping girl, 13. Kieran Hayler had denied rape, sexual assault and sexual activity with a child at his trial.

Ukraine says it carried out first drone airlift of wounded soldier from front line. The serviceman was surrounded by landmines and enemy drones so a ground rescue was not possible, Ukraine's military says.
Clean up begins after French riots but police remain. Outside of Paris, Marseille saw some of the worst damage, with shop owners reporting more than 600 premises having been looted.
Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say. A truck carrying people to a funeral and a market alleged to be supplying fuel to the RSF were targeted.

BBC inside Australian court as man charged with attacking MP stays silent in first hearing. BBC's Katy Watson describes what unfolded in Wangaratta as 43-year-old Brendan Nugent appeared before court over the alleged attack of Helen Haines.
Pakistan arrests man wanted by US over $126m postage fraud case. Faheem Akram allegedly sold more than 5 million fake postage labels for a fixed price of $2 a piece.
Gambia to pay victims of Yahya Jammeh's rule from proceeds of his seized US mansion. The Gambia has confirmed receiving $2.5m from the sale of the house in Maryland.
Elon Musk confirms he is considering merging Tesla and SpaceX. Musk says special committees within both companies have been formed to look at a possible mega-merger.
Macron accuses foreign leaders of exploiting French riots. The comment is an apparent swipe at Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump, who both face elections in coming weeks.
Family of prison officer killed by IRA receives state apology. Brian Stack was crossing a street in Dublin in 1983 when he was shot in the back of the neck and died 18 months later.
'Targeted' attack on much-loved MP leaves Australian town heartbroken. Locals describe the MP, who had to have both legs amputated, as a genuinely kind person who fought for the community.
India 'cockroach' leaders who called on election chief to quit are freed from jail. Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were accused of breaking into an unauthorised protest venue in Delhi.

Rosenberg: Russia agrees to Ukraine talks but sees little to talk about in new peace push. President Vladimir Putin does not feel under pressure right now to end the war, the BBC's Russia Editor writes.
Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery. Test results have confirmed his diagnosis as a lung adenocarcinoma that was localised.
Ex-prosecutor charged with treason in Mexico over US drug raid. César Jáuregui Moreno is accused of allowing US agents to join a raid on a suspected drugs lab in April.

Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees to US call to resume Ukraine peace talks. Moscow says it is "ready in principle" to resume peace talks and US President Donald Trump says the world is "the closest we've been" to ending the war.
Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy. The fine is the largest to date against Facebook's owner, larger than an $18bn deal with California.

Japan is known for world-class events - but the Asian Games were chaotic. Hotel chaos, transport mishaps and diplomatic blunders cast a spotlight on organisers and the firm hired to deliver the games.

Why is a peat fire so bad? BBC is in Indonesia to find out. The BBC's Liza Tambunan is in central Kalimantan, to explain what peat is and why Indonesia is facing its worst wildfire season in a decade.

New Mexico sues Epstein lawyer and accountant, accusing them of hiding his sex crimes. Both men have denied having any knowledge of Epstein's crimes and their attorney rejected the lawsuit as "categorically false".
Airbnb hosts can no longer make guests strip beds and wash dishes under new rules. The updated policy will apply to all reservations booked on the accommodation site on or after 20 November.

Vance tells Republicans to 'stop whining' about controversial Ohio attack ad. The ad by Ohio Republican Vivek Ramaswamy features his Democratic rival's estranged mother, who she has not seen since her stepfather was charged with sexual abuse in her childhood.
Trump's green card curbs test Indian tech workers' American dream. With immigration curbs and tech firms cutting foreign hiring, US residency is becoming a distant dream for many Indians.
The real reasons there are so few young politicians in the US. No country for young men and women: why do older politicians seem to have such a tight grip on the US political system?
US embassy accuses Canada of election meddling ahead of midterms. Prime Minister Mark Carney dismissed the claim, noting that US initiated trade actions against Canada.
No order, no seat: Starbucks China rolls out new store policy. Starbucks says it is improving customers' in-store experience as it competes with homegrown rivals.

How Arab parties could hold critical balance of power in Israeli election. Disaffection has often driven down turnout among Arab Israelis, but there is a strong push to get rid of the right-wing governing coalition.
Some New Yorkers back ban on horse-drawn carriages, but drivers fear for incomes. As councillors prepare to banish the vehicles, views in Central Park are divided over the 160-year-old tradition.
Two killed in attack on airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, authorities say. It is the latest in a series of attacks by the Houthi movement which have targeted airports and other sites in the kingdom.
How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders?. Many view it as one of the most pivotal elections in Israel's history, with global implications.
Police investigate Married at First Sight Australia after 'inappropriate' allegations. New South Wales Police say inquiries took place "following a report of inappropriate content being shared".
Nigeria's first Ebola patient holidayed in Uganda, officials say. The wife of a diplomat based in Abuja travelled to Kampala for a vacation.
Celebrity shark guided out of South Korea canal refuses to swim out to sea. Bukangi the shark became an unlikely sensation after it was spotted in a canal in Busan weeks ago.
El Salvador's president threatens Haitian gangs over military hostages. Four members of the so-called Gang Suppression Force have been missing since Sunday.
First human case of Shamonda virus detected in France, officials say. The disease, which usually affects cattle, has been identified in a patient who died in early October.
Moment man rescued from sinking car by Australian TV reporter. Journalist Will Murray describes how he and a bystander saved an SUV driver from his vehicle.
Two European women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya. The Swiss government told the BBC that the freed national was on her way back to Switzerland.
What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber-security scramble?. AI uncovered long-hidden programming flaws, triggering a rare global cyber-security response.
At least four dead after storm brings flooding to southern France. The deaths include two women found drowned in a cellar in the Bouches-du-Rhône region.

Vital Central Valley flood control levees are poorly maintained, state watchdog finds. Nearly a third of local agencies maintaining Central Valley levees have performed “unacceptable” upkeep, some for years, yet the Department of Water Resources hasn’t taken over as state law requires. State water managers dispute the findings, saying maintenance is only one factor in flood risk and takeovers can cost tens of millions of dollars up front.

California decision to pull Tahoe schools from Nevada athletics imperils more than trans athletes. California ordered Tahoe-Truckee Unified to exit the Nevada athletics conference over a conflict with transgender athlete rules. A parent says officials failed to account for what that means for families in the snowy Sierra.

Trump’s crackdown on immigrant voting in California is a ploy to influence election. President Donald Trump wants California to segregate 20,000 ballots, claiming they may come from noncitizens. Federal officers charged 28 suspects with voter fraud this week.

What to know about California’s other tax-the-rich measure: Prop. 3. Voters first passed the tax in 2012, then renewed it in 2016. Now, its supporters are asking voters to make it permanent before it expires in 2031.

Big California state worker strike set to begin today. Perhaps today is not the best day to go to the DMV. California state workers are planning a one-day strike today in multiple cities including Sacramento, San Francisco and Los Angeles. They’re protesting what they say are unfair labor practices by Gov. Gavin Newsom’s administration. The work stoppage could affect services at the DMV, unemployment […]

‘Es algo que raya en lo absurdo’. California lucha contra la demanda de Trump para anular 20,000 papeletas. This article is also available in English. Read it here. El fiscal general de California pidió a un juez federal que bloqueara los esfuerzos de la administración Trump para obligar al estado a apartar hasta 20,000 papeletas que, según las autoridades federales, podrían haber sido enviadas por correo a personas que no son ciudadanas estadounidenses. […]

Thousands of California state workers walk off the job in contract dispute with Newsom. The largest union in California state government held a one-day strike, drawing thousands of workers off the job. It's pressing Gov. Gavin Newsom for raises and more flexibility to work from home.

California cities pull the plug on data centers after state regulations don’t scale up fast enough. Despite seven new statewide laws regulating data centers, at least 26 resolutions, moratoriums, or bans on data centers have been passed or proposed in California since June.

Why the fate of California’s wealth tax could be decided well after the election. Proposition 40 has a gauntlet to run to succeed, including surviving two poison-pill propositions. If it passes, it will probably be challenged in court.

Medi-Cal cuts could push seniors and people with disabilities off of coverage. Julia Feinberg feels like she’s living in a sinister version of Groundhog Day. For the second year in a row California lawmakers have made it tougher for seniors and people with disabilities to qualify for state-funded health benefits. Feinberg, 37, who has a degenerative neuromuscular disorder, said without Medi-Cal she would be confined to a […]
Daylight Saving Time Ends Soon. Here’s When the Clocks Go Back an Hour. Why do we “fall back” in November? We answer your questions.
The iPhone Duo Will Run iOS 27.1 at Launch on Friday. Apple said update has features built specifically for the new iPhone design.

The iOS 27 Setting That Can Flag a Scam While You’re Still on the Phone. Apple’s new scam protection works on the device, returns a simple risk rating to supported apps and takes a few taps to enable in Privacy & Security.
Is It Worth Getting AppleCare for the iPhone Duo? Repairs Could Cost as Much as the Phone Itself. If something happens, you could be facing a $1,500 repair on top of the foldable’s $2,000 price.

Today’s NYT Wordle Hints, Answer and Help for Wednesday, Oct. 21, #1950. Need a Wordle hint today? Get spoiler-free hints for NYT Wordle No. 1,950 on Wednesday, Oct. 21, then the answer, plus yesterday’s word.
This Viral Indie Horror Game Is Coming to Xbox Game Pass Just in Time for Halloween. Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade is also coming to the service soon.

Investigation Reveals How TikTok Executives Ignored Internal Child-Safety Warnings. NPR reports that TikTok staff raised the alarm on youth bypassing age restrictions as well as being sexually exploited on the platform.

Minecraft and Domino’s Team Up for Block-Shaped Pizza, In-Game Freebies. Customers are randomly awarded an in-game code for either a Domino’s skin, cape or cheesy cube pet. The pizza will come in one of six Minecraft-themed boxes.

My Favorite Budget Camera Brand Is Finally Getting 4K Plus and a Mile-Long Range. Blink’s newest line of cameras includes features the brand has never tried before, but prices remain affordable starting at $50.
PHP Vulnerabilities Could Put Much of the Internet at Risk, Experts Warn. Up to 70% of all the websites on the internet could be affected.
I’m Baffled by Oppo’s Find X10 Pro Max, but I Love It Anyway. Oppo launched two excellent phones within six months of each other. I’m confused, but maybe you can figure it out.

Supernatural Restart: The VR Fitness App Is Back as VR Itself Starts to Change. Exclusive: Supernatural is relaunching in early access and could expand beyond Meta Quest headsets. Meanwhile, Meta VR Glasses could shape what comes next for fitness.
Ohio State Makes a Stink by Digitally Sending Scents. The scent-sending technology could be used in online shopping, healhcare diagnoses and just for fun.
The ESA’s Euclid Telescope Discovered a New Comet Completely by Accident. It was identified in Euclid telescope imagery using software designed to detect moving objects.
Tech Issues Are on the Ballot This Midterm Election Season: What to Know. AI, data centers and Flock cameras are key tech policy issues shaping the campaigns, candidates and voters.
Apple’s iPhone Duo Should Get Reachability Accessibility in an Upcoming Update. The $1,999 foldable phone is harder to use for left-handed people and those with smaller hands.
The 3-in-1 Alloop Wearable Could Replace Both Your Wellness Wristband and Ring. The Alloop Trio also comes with a personal AI health agent.
Lawsuits Allege Delivery Robots Recorded Biometric Data Without Permission. As delivery robots roll through cities like Chicago, they’re fueling fears about unregulated surveillance in public spaces.
Google Chrome Will Notify You If You’re on a Scam Website. You’ll need to opt into Chrome’s Enhanced Protection mode to use the new features.
AI and Data Centers Will Impact Midterm Voting, According to Experts. Americans are mostly negative on AI and oppose new data centers near them, another poll shows.

Tons of People Are Apparently Asking Meta’s Muse AI Agent to Shop for Them. A quarter of Meta Muse’s 10 million users are shopping online via the AI agent with an average spend of $200 per purchase, according to Mark Zuckerberg.
EA Shutters BioWare, Creator of Mass Effect, Dragon Age, KOTOR and More. The legendary studio has been shut down just months after EA was acquired by a private equity consortium.
A Privacy Company Just Saved the Clearest Flock Surveillance Map I’ve Seen. The creator of Proton Mail now hosts a powerful, professional Flock camera mapping tool on its site.
Apple Limits iPhone Duo Purchases to 2 Foldable Phones Per Person. For the first time in many years, Apple is limiting how many phones you can buy.

Test Driving an iPhone Duo? 6 Things to Try at the Apple Store. Apple’s first foldable has a lot going for it, but there may be some compromises you aren’t expecting. See for yourself if the Duo is for you.

BBC Merges TV & Audio Commissioning Teams Amid Plan To Cut 100 Content Roles. EXCLUSIVE: The BBC will merge TV and audio commissioning teams across comedy and other genres amid plans to close around 100 roles in its content unit. In an internal memo earlier this week, BBC content chief Kate Phillips told colleagues that her department will make “tough” choices to support the corporation’s belt-tightening. Phillips announced that […]

Canal+ “Making Progress” In Opposing French VAT Hike That It Says Would Force Subs Increases & Cuts. Canal+ has “made progress” in opposing a controversial proposal in France that would double the VAT rate on TV subscriptions from 10% to 20%. Delivering a Q3 trading update, the French major said it has support from “cinema organisations, federations and leagues” and will continue fighting the rate increase tooth and nail. “The Group has […]

EXCLUSIVE: Billy Porter, Leslie Jones and Phoebe Robinson are launching a comedy podcast exploring live performance. The 48-part weekly comedy series, Places, Dahlingz!, will see theater icon Porter, theater critic Jones and theater convert and comedian Robinson sitting down with Broadway stars such as Shoshana Bean, Ariana DeBose and Renée Elise Goldsberry. Billed as “part […]

‘Harry Potter’ Production Accounts Reveal Clue About Budget For HBO Series. Harry Potter is on course to be among the most expensive series ever made by HBO. A source familiar with the adaptation of J.K. Rowling’s beloved books confirmed that the Potter series will rank alongside the final season of Game of Thrones and The Last of Us, as production accounts provided a clue about the […]

‘Normal People’ Stars Paul Mescal & Daisy Edgar-Jones Among Signatories Of Open Letter Supporting Sally Rooney After UK Book Ban. Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones have signed an open letter in support of their Normal People scribe Sally Rooney. Earlier this month, it was confirmed that Rooney’s books would be withdrawn from sale in the UK over her support of the banned protest group Palestine Action. Palestine Action is a pro-Palestinian direct action group that […]

‘The Day’: First Look At Minnie Driver As Hostage Negotiator In Paramount+ Drama ‘The Day’. EXCLUSIVE: Here’s a first look at Minnie Driver as a hostage negotiator in Paramount+’s tense heist thriller The Day. We’ve got a batch of images for the eight-part British drama, which is based on 2018 Belgian series De Dag and alos stars the likes of Luca Pasqualino and Louisa Harland. TV Festival Unveils Dates, Venues & Advisory Chair For First-Ever Greater Manchester Edition. The UK’s biggest TV Festival has revealed the dates it will officially launch in Greater Manchester for the first time, with Sony international productions boss Wayne Garvie aboard as advisory chair. The TV Festival will move one week back from its traditional Edinburgh slot to the week after the August Bank Holiday from Tuesday August […]

Laura Birn Leading Sports Doping Thriller Series ‘Disqualified’ From Banijay Finland & Journalist Johanna Aatsalo. EXCLUSIVE: Foundation actress Laura Birn is leading a sports doping thriller series from Banijay Finland and journalist Johanna Aatsalo. Disqualified is being presented at the MIA Market in Rome today as a TV drama inspired by one of real-life events surrounding Finland’s most notorious sporting scandals. The series is based on Aatsalo’s reporting, which became […]

Charades Boards Juho Kuosmanen’s ‘Dream Come True’ As Production Wraps Across Europe. EXCLUSIVE: Charades has acquired international rights to Dream Come True, the third feature film by Finnish director Juho Kuosmanen, best known for his 2021 Cannes Grand Prix-winning Compartment No. 6. Production has wrapped on the film, which was shot in Denmark, Finland and France. The film is said to tell the story of 43-year-old Rasmus, […]

Comcast Q3: Record-Breaking ‘Odyssey’, Profitable Peacock Fuel NBCU Spinoff Momentum. Odysseus and his intrepid crew sailed through Comcast’s latest quarter as Universal surpassed $5 billion at the global box office, led by the The Odyssey, now Universal’s highest-grossing film of all time. The Christopher Nolan smash based on Homer’s epic has grossed nearly $1.9 billion worldwide since its July opening and set all sort of […]

Andy Burnham Becomes First UK Prime Minister To Join ‘Celebrity Gogglebox’. Plenty of Prime Ministers have been watched on Channel 4’s Gogglebox, but none have bedecked the famous sofas until now. Tomorrow, Andy Burnham will appear from 10 Downing Street on Gogglebox for Stand Up To Cancer sat alongside his old friend Steve Rotheram, the Mayor of Liverpool. Check out a tease below. Appearing at 9.05 […]

Multiple witnesses in the Russell Brand trial have claimed that their friend was in physical pain and “extremely distressed” after she was allegedly anally raped by the Despicable Me star in 2009. US Army showing interest in G/ATOR missile-killing radar, Northrop says. Northrop Grumman’s new multi-mission radar system has earned high marks from Marine Corps leadership. The U.S. Army has taken notice.

Australia gets the ball rolling on medium-range air defense. Recognizing the massive gap, Canberra has launched a formal tender for a medium-range, ground-based air defense solution for the Australian Army.

US Army acquisition command awards contracts worth $6.8B in 2026. The Mission and Installation Contracting Command awarded 21,450 contracts in fiscal 2026 valued at $6.8 billion in total, a boost from the year prior.
US Army Cyber Command charts course for human-AI equilibrium. U.S. Army Cyber Command is constantly refining human oversight of artificial intelligence, Lt. Gen. Christopher Eubank said last week.

Groups seek clarity on motive behind Pentagon’s study of women in combat. Citing concerns about Hegseth’s views on the topic, the lawsuit asks for records showing the scope, purpose, methodology and anticipated use of the study.

Shield AI software cuts autonomous flight development to six weeks. Shield AI said this week that its Hivemind software helped Honeywell Aerospace achieve autonomous flight after six weeks, down from 54 weeks.
US Army competition explores military uses for humanoid robots. They're still a long way off from mass-producing Terminators.

Pentagon, BAE sign deal for up to 25,000 precision-guided munition kits a year. The Pentagon and BAE Systems signed a framework agreement for up to 25,000 Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System, or APKWS, guidance kits a year.

Tip of the spear, or stranded on beaches? Chinese planners dissect USMC Pacific posture. Understanding these dynamics, American leaders should recalibrate and opt to rely less on forward defense, writes analyst Lyle Goldstein.
Ukraine’s Zelenskyy says US decisions on Ukraine hard to explain. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy laments delayed arms shipments, saying the Trump administration is dragging its feet.
US Navy, Gecko Robotics surge AI maintenance contract to $300M. Gecko Robotics uses drones, wall-climbing robots and fixed sensors to gather data on components, decks, welds and hulls.

Hegseth discusses Iran with Netanyahu in unannounced visit to Israel, officials say. Netanyahu and Hegseth discussed “the threats in the region” and the U.S.-Israel partnership in dealing both offensively and defensively with those threats.

China built more than twice naval tonnage of US in 2024-25: Euronaval. China built more than twice the naval tonnage of the U.S. in the 2024-25 period, narrowing the gap between the two countries’ navies, a new report says.
US Air Force F-22 pilot controls unmanned FQ-44 in flight. The fighter jet’s pilot served as an airborne “quarterback” and gave high-level directives to an Anduril-made Collaborative Combat Aircraft.
US Army support for Golden Dome missile shield takes shape. A U.S. Army air defense unit has been "earmarked" for support of the Golden Dome for America project, an Army official confirmed.

Medal of Honor recipient Dakota Meyer tapped as Barracks Task Force senior advisor. Medal of Honor recipient Dakota Meyer was selected as Secretary Hegseth's senior advisor and will visit military installations across the country.

Europe weighs giving utilities, infrastructure companies more powers to bring down drones. Offials are worried that drone attacks could knock out power to millions of people — as has happened frequently in Ukraine after Russian strikes.
US Marine Corps makes Maven available service-wide. The service made the AI-enabled battlefield management system available to all commands and organizations within the service.

Timing to roll out US Army’s NGC2 depends on funds, commander says. The head of the Army formation responsible for fielding the Next Generation Command and Control system said the timeline depends on resources available.

German military raises sabotage threat level amid warning of Russian attacks: report. German forces themselves could face attacks at home, according to a classified internal analysis reported by public broadcaster WDR and newspaper SZ.
Got milk? US Army refines its pasteurization power. Thirteen U.S. Army Veterinary Corps officers milked a trip to Denmark last month, completing Europe Dairy Pasteurization Audit Training.

Pentagon AI oversight office struggles to keep pace with department’s ambitions, GAO finds. The Pentagon office tapped in 2022 to oversee the military’s responsible use of AI had filled just three of 10 authorized positions as of February 2026.
US Air Force outlines the fighter fleet it needs by 2035. A new Air Force report calls for 1,509 combat-coded fighters by 2035, with F-35s making up 40% of the fleet and F-47s replacing F-22s.

Ukraine to be able to buy military supplies via NATO agency: report. The deal comes amid worsening U.S.-Ukraine relations since U.S. President Trump announced a diesel export deal with Russia this month to lower U.S. prices.

UK’s Royal Navy has ‘serious’ anti-submarine warfare gap, committee finds. The Royal Navy has a “serious anti-submarine warfare gap” that weakens the U.K.'s ability to respond to Russia’s submarine and underwater sabotage threats.
Apple iPhone Duo review: A first-class foldable. Even though it's heavy and expensive, Apple's first foldable handset is a treat for iPhone users unwilling to switch to Android.

Here's how SpaceX plans to catch Starship's upper stage for the first time. SpaceX has released a demo showing how it intends to catch Starship's upper stage, which could happen as soon as next month.
How to spot a white label gadget, and why that's important. Sometimes the same product is sold under multiple brands, which means you might not be getting the best gear.

Stranger Than Heaven builds its identity as Like A Dragon's more relentless spin-off. We played several hours of Sega's next big crime-thriller, and so far the Like a Dragon series is getting its most bold entry to date.
A permanent Pokémon store will open in London, with more locations outside Asia to follow. The new retail location is set to open by 2029.
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max hands-on: Triple 200-megapixel cameras but few surprises. Trying to fill a OnePlus-shaped hole, Oppo plays it a little safe.
Now you can chat with Gemini while using Google Maps through CarPlay. Just tap the new Gemini icon to get started.
Supernatural's VR exercise app has relaunched on Meta VR headsets. It's in early access and subscriptions cost $20 per month or $200 each year.
Sony's PlayStation Pulse headset arrives on November 19 for $100. Pre-orders open on October 29.
There's a new Apple Music logo and it looks like ripples in water. Maybe they should use it as the app logo instead.
EA is shutting down BioWare and cutting around 400 jobs. Skate studio Full Circle will be be reduced to "a more focused, smaller team," while a Sims project has been paused.
Xbox is previewing paid cloud gaming for players without Game Pass. Here come new rate limits.
Meta ordered to cough up $25 billion in New Mexico privacy case. The case stemmed from the nearly decade-old Cambridge Analytica scandal.
Government websites in the EU and Canada taken offline over PHP vulnerability. All websites using PHP should update to the latest security patch.
Claude Duet is Anthropic's answer to Meta Muse and OpenAI Dots. Anthropic subscribers in the US can join a waitlist to try the company's new agent.

Your guide to Proposition 3: Making a high-income tax extension permanent. Prop 3 would make permanent an expiring income tax on the top 2% of California taxpayers that provides money for education, healthcare and other services.

Your guide to Proposition 4: Allowing public campaign financing in California. Prop 4 would repeal California's 1988 ban on public campaign financing, allowing state and local governments to create programs for candidates seeking office.

Your guide to Proposition 5: Big changes to recall elections in California. Prop 5 would make major changes to how recall elections are conducted in California, especially affecting the office of governor.

Your guide to Proposition 37: Loans for middle-income homeowners. If passed by voters, Proposition 37 would create a down payment loan program for middle-income homebuyers. The state's housing finance agency would loan up to 17% of a home sale price.

Your guide to Proposition 38: Immunology and immunotherapy research funding. Prop 38 aims to fund immunotherapy research to prevent and cure diseases through bonds. An opponent says it is a debt-financed model that prioritizes a few diseases.

Your guide to Proposition 39: Stricter voter ID requirements. Prop 39 brings the national debate around U.S. election integrity home to California by proposing stricter new voter identification and citizenship verification requirements for state elections.

Your guide to Proposition 41: Special tax audit proposal could block billionaire tax. Prop 41 would require audits for new state special taxes and prohibit certain new state taxes. It also could nullify the billionaire tax.

Your guide to Proposition 42: Tax ban on retirement, personal savings. Prop 42 would ban new taxes on various forms of personal savings and certain retroactive taxes and also could block a proposed billionaire tax.

Your guide to Proposition 43: Voting thresholds for local special taxes. Prop 43 would require two-thirds voter approval for all local special taxes, including citizen-sponsored measures that California courts have allowed to pass with a simple majority.

Your guide to Proposition 44: Federally funded health clinic spending. Prop 44 asks voters to require federally funded community health centers to spend at least 90% of their total annual revenue on "program services advancing their charitable purpose."

Your guide to Proposition 45: Faster CEQA review for housing and infrastructure. Prop 45 seeks to overhaul the law often blamed for delaying construction and driving up its cost: the California Environmental Quality Act.

Your guide to L.A. City Charter Amendment PRK: More money for parks. Los Angeles City Charter Amendment PRK would double the amount of money set aside for L.A.'s park system over 10 years. City leaders would need to find a way to pay for those increases later on.

Your guide to L.A. City Charter Amendment PRT: Greater public insight into airport, harbor departments. Los Angeles City Charter Amendment PRT would affect the city's departments of airports, harbor and water and power, which operate as self-funding businesses.

Your guide to L.A. City Charter Amendment SC: Board of education campaign finance rules. Los Angeles City Charter Amendment SC would clarify language in the city charter to make clear candidates for the LAUSD Board of Education face the same campaign finance rules as mayoral candidates.

Hugo Morán, secretario de Estado de Medio Ambiente: "El zapatero y el técnico de lavadora volverán a nuestras vidas". Morán advierte de que el Gobierno "no acepta" que una hipotética simplificación normativa en aras de la productividad suponga "desregulación porque siempre significa desprotección ambiental" España, incapaz de cumplir con la ley: estas son las comunidades que más y menos reciclan El secretario de Estado de Medio Ambiente, Hugo Morán, ha vaticinado que la reparación y reutilización de productos —pilares de la economía circular— es una realidad imparable que va a imponerse. “El zapatero y el técnico de la lavadora volverán a nuestras vidas”, ha afirmado Morán durante el V Foro ReGenera de elDiario.es. También ha advertido Morán de que, a pesar de la corriente antiverde que se expande en aras de la productividad económica, “el Gobierno no acepta una simplificación [de normas] que suponga una desregulación porque eso siempre significa una desprotección ambiental”. En este sentido, a preguntas del redactor jefe de Economía de elDiario.es, Serafí del Arco, el secretario de Estado ha insistido en que “la sociedad europea no está dispuesta a retroceder en derechos. De la misma manera que no acepta retroceder en derechos de las mujeres no acepta perder derechos ambientales. Europa es generadora de derechos que, luego, se expanden a más países”. Así ha contestado a la idea de que la regulación verde es un lastre para las empresas y su competitividad. También ha admitido que el consumidor tendrá que afrontar una posible subida de precios de productos cuando se rediseñen para que duren más y puedan ser reutilizados Poca circularidad España reutiliza un 8% de las materias que aplica en sus procesos de producción. Está por debajo de la media europea que supera el 11%. Para Hugo Morán, el problema nace de que “durante décadas se nos ha inculcado que la calidad de vida depende de la capacidad de consumo”. Es decir, cuánto más se compra mejor vida se tiene. “Hay que cambiar de ropa, de móvil, de automóvil y mostrarlo”, ha indicado el político. De la misma manera, ha reconocido que, hasta ahora, se ha puesto mucho el foco en el consumidor y poco en las empresas. “Era más fácil” pedir a los ciudadanos que reciclen que obligar a las empresas a que produzcan bienes que duren más. “La reacción contra los cambios en la manera de producir de los sectores industriales es más difícil. Y tienen más capacidad de movilizar potencia publicitaria”. En este sentido, Morán ha indicado que España tiene mucho margen y un mercado delante en la reutilización de materias. Por ejemplo “los materiales utilizados en las energías renovables, el textil —que hasta ahora externalizaba la gestión de residuos y los tiraba en el patio trasero de los países en vías de desarrollo— y en la construcción”. Se trata de recuperar materia prima en lugar de importar nueva. Sin embargo, Hugo Morán se ha quejado de que, hasta la gestión de residuos se haya convertido en materia de batalla cultural e ideológica. “Si un céntimo más en la tasa de basuras se ha convertido en el eje de la campaña electoral y puede decidir quién gobierna un municipio, imaginad cómo se afronta esa materia”. En este sentido ha aludido a la polémica suscitada por la inclusión explícita y segregada de la tasa de basuras municipal (obligatoria por la ley europea). “Cualquiera entiende que un sevicio de recogida de basuras hay que pagarlo. Y ya se pagaba lo que ocurre es que se camuflaba. Salía del impuesto de circulación o esaba en el IBI”. Preguntado específicamente sobre el asunto del biogás —el combustible que se obtiene desde los desechos orgánicos de la ganadería—, el secretario de Estado ha explicado que “no puede significar una barra libre para los empresarios y hay riesgo de que suceda”. ¿A qué se refiere? A que “el sector ganadero sigue teniendo la misma responsabilidad de gestión de sus desechos. No puede ser que el biometano sirva para esconder el problema de la gestión de estiércol. La expansión del biogás no puede ser que cada uno haga lo que quiera, sino una solución empresarialmente viable, ciudadanamente aceptable y ambientalmente sostenible”. Para cerrar, el secretario de Estado ha insistido en que, ante la cada vez “más inestable” disponibilidad de agua, la reutilización cobra importancia crucial y ha sentenciado: “El ahorro, la eficiencia y la reutilización son los embalses que nos suministrarán en el futuro”.

Un tema Al día reúne a más de 1.300 personas en el teatro: “No estamos solos ni somos pocos”. El podcast de elDiario.es llena el Teatro Lope de Vega de Madrid con un recorrido emocionante por los momentos compartidos en cinco temporadas La grabación de este directo estará disponible gratis a partir del jueves 8 de octubre en Amazon Music Un encuentro emocionante, un relato sobre la conexión íntima entre la vida y la política, un homenaje a todas las personas necesarias para que el periodismo tenga sentido. El primer gran directo de Un tema Al día ha reunido a más de 1.300 personas en el Teatro Lope de Vega de Madrid, confirmando que el podcast de elDiario.es no es solo el más escuchado en su formato, sino que cuenta con la complicidad de una enorme comunidad de oyentes, que acudieron sin saber muy bien qué se iban a encontrar. “¿Cómo hemos llegado hasta aquí?”, arrancaba Juanlu Sánchez, subdirector de elDiario.es y director de Un tema Al día. A partir de esa pregunta, el guión fue tejiendo con sonidos un relato que pasaba de lo personal a lo político, de la memoria a la esperanza, del auge de la extrema derecha a las protestas por la vivienda. Historias que han recordado lo que el equipo y los oyentes han compartido a lo largo de más de mil episodios, con espacio también para el humor. “No solo tenemos oyentes”, recordó Juanlu Sánchez, sino una comunidad que cada mañana se reúne “para sostenerle la mirada al mundo”. El recorrido terminó con la aparición por sorpresa en el escenario de Oksana Horin y Kayed Hammad, dos voces conocidas por la comunidad de oyentes de Un tema Al día. Ella relató los primeros días de la invasión rusa de Ucrania; él compartió desde Gaza la vida de su familia bajo los bombardeos, el hambre y los desplazamientos. “Queremos agradecer y rendir homenaje a las personas que en el momento más difícil de sus vidas decidieron hablar con periodistas de elDiario.es”, explicó Juanlu Sánchez. La conversación con ambos conectó aquellas grabaciones con sus vidas de ahora y con una pregunta que atraviesa todo el episodio: cómo mirar al futuro después de lo vivido. La sorpresa del día fue la presencia de Oksana Horin y Kayed Hammad, dos voces conocidas por la comunidad de oyentes de Un tema Al día, junto a Juanlu Sánchez. Este directo en Madrid podrá escucharse gratis a partir del próximo jueves 8 de octubre en Amazon Music. Será el primero de una serie de contenidos especiales y entrevistas de Un tema Al día que se publicarán en Amazon Music cada 15 días. Un tema Al día, el podcast diario de actualidad de elDiario.es, cumple su sexta temporada con más de un millón de escuchas al mes y más de 200.000 suscriptores en plataformas de audio. Dirigido por Juanlu Sánchez, cuenta con el trabajo de Marcos García Santonja, Carmen Ibáñez, Pedro Nogales e Izaskun Pérez y con la participación de la redacción y las ediciones locales de elDiario.es. Un volcán, cinco años después: ¿en qué ha cambiado la vida de los palmeros?. El podcast ‘Hogar de cenizas’ habla con los afectados del volcán para entender por qué nos cuesta tanto construir un hogar Episodio 4 - ¿Hay hogares que vale la pena dejar ir? El 19 de septiembre de 2021, Eva tuvo que marcharse de su casa, porque a pocos kilómetros montaña arriba había erupcionado un volcán. Cinco años después, aunque su casa finalmente se librase de la lava, sigue viviendo en un contenedor. ¿ Qué ha fallado en La Palma para que 110 familias no hayan podido reconstruir su vida? Rayco, que vivía en el centro de Todoque , ha comprado una finca con un pajero para reformar en Mazo, a 50 minutos de su antigua casa. “Cada vez que quiero socializar tengo que atravesar media isla. Si viviese en el Oeste me sentiría más acogido, allí es donde me crie, pero está todo carísimo”. Vicente entraba en su casa cada semana para barrer ceniza. No barría el suelo, barría el tejado: su vivienda había quedado totalmente sepultada por la lluvia de piroclasto. Limpiaba la ceniza, sabiendo que tras marcharse, su casa volvería a quedar tapada. “Llegué un día y me di cuenta de que ya no había casa. Tenía que descubrirla yo. Tenía que desenterrarla”. Vicente dejaba unos palos sobresaliendo de la chimenea para saber, al regresar, donde comenzar a excavar de nuevo y no perder de vista la casa bajo un manto de ceniza. Vicente, uno de los afectados por el volcán de La Palma. El volcán Tajogaite cumplió el pasado 19 de septiembre cinco años, pero no todas las familias de la isla han podido recuperar su hogar. En total, la lava se llevó 1.600 casas y dos barrios enteros -El Paraíso y Todoque- que han quedado bajo un manto de roca negra. Por vivienda afectada, el Gobierno central ha concedido una ayuda de 60.000 euros, el Gobierno canario, 30.000 más, y el Cabildo otros 10.000. Quién tuviera la vivienda asegurada, ha podido recibir del Consorcio el valor de su casa. Pero para recibir todo esto, lo esencial es tener una casa. Y sobre el papel, muchos afectados no la tenían. ¿Cómo es posible? En La Palma, donde el salario mínimo es regla y la mayor parte del territorio no es urbanizable -por lo tanto, el que hay es caro- muchos vecinos levantan sus casas poco a poco, a lo largo de los años, partiendo de pequeños cuartos de apero en una finca o en un terreno rústico. Y nunca llegan a regularizar esa vivienda. Hay quién diría que es picardía. Para muchos es necesidad. En este contexto, mucha gente no ha podido siquiera demostrar que han sido afectados por un volcán porque no vivían oficialmente en la zona. En La Palma, el volcán no solo se lleva cuatro paredes. Se lleva el esfuerzo de años de levantar una casa, piedra a piedra, y se lleva a los vecinos que han ayudado a levantarla. Porque cuando la mano de obra es cara, en La Palma las “gallofas” ganan terreno y es la comunidad quién ayuda en la obra. Hace cinco años, el volcán se llevó las paredes, pero también separó a los vecinos. Calle de casas contenedor de los afectados por el volcán de La Palma. Los contenedores No son casos aislados, sino que se trata de uno de los principales problemas de esta erupción, y da respuesta a por qué, cinco años después, 110 familias siguen viviendo en los “barracones”, que se construyeron como medidas supuestamente temporales. La vida en estos contenedores no es sencilla: quién vive ahí ahora, antes del volcán solía vivir en una casa terrera, con su huerta y animales. Los contenedores tienen unos 50 metros cuadrados y están situados en un parking. En la localidad de Los Llanos, los vecinos se quejan de la falta de insonorización y de aislamiento, tanto del frío como del calor. Eva cuenta que no es capaz de sentir el contenedor como un hogar porque “no estoy en mi ambiente, porque no puedo moverme. De aquí al sofá, del sofá a la cama, de la cama al sofá. Salir no salgo, porque todo el mundo ahí afuera está con la oreja pegada”. Viviendas en contenedores para personas afectadas por el volcán, que humea detrás, al fondo. Otra dificultad por la que están pasando los afectados es la adaptación a un formato de vida no acorde con sus costumbres. “Vivíamos entre familias y nos llevábamos muy bien con todos los vecinos”, cuentan dos hermanas de La Laguna, barrio que se perdió parcialmente. En los lugares afectados, lo más habitual era vivir en lugares con huerto o jardín, lo que contrasta con el reducido espacio del contenedor. “Árboles frutales, naranjos, orquídeas. Teníamos de todo. Nosotras estábamos acostumbradas a vivir en casas terreras. Y eso está debajo del volcán”. Eva concluye: “El container no está para vivir personas. Esto es de chapa. La chapa está pensada para meter muebles y animales, y nosotros no somos eso”. El estatus de damnificado Los vecinos damnificados han podido construir de manera legal en terreno rústico. Pero, ¿quién se considera damnificado del volcán? Ahí radica otro de los grandes problemas. Rayco no se considera damnificado a efectos legales, ya que su casa estaba a nombre de sus padres. Por tanto, no ha podido acogerse a las ayudas y facilidades para construir que ofrecen las Administraciones. Lo mismo le sucede a aquellos que, tras el fallecimiento del propietario original, no actualizaron el registro de la propiedad. Si el propietario de la vivienda está muerto, sus herederos -hijos, sobre todo- no han podido recibir las ayudas por la pérdida de la casa, aun estando empadronados en ella. Vecinos desalojando sus casas en La Palma durante la erupción. Vicente ha tardado tres años en recibir la consideración de afectado. Su casa sigue en pie, aunque quedase sepultada bajo la ceniza. “Se ha pagado el valor de lo perdido bajo la lava. Pero ¿qué ocurre con estas viviendas que están deterioradas, con grietas, no hay paredes, no hay servicios...? Para esto no ha habido ninguna dotación”. Vicente no puede habitar su casa, porque hasta su barrio en Las Manchas todavía no llega ninguna carretera, ni agua o luz. Es un barrio todavía sepultado por la ceniza. Tan solo algunas viviendas como la suya sobresalen de entre el desierto negro. Muchos vecinos denuncian violencia burocrática. “ Vas al Ayuntamiento y todo son problemas. Como si no fueras afectada, ¿sabes?”, cuenta Esther, que perdió la casa el último día de erupción y quiso reconstruir sobre la lava, en su propiedad. “ Para construir, tuve que pedir que me quitaran de la zona de exclusión. Me quitaron, después me volvieron a poner, sin dar explicaciones. Pedíamos permiso para aplanar, para quitar la lava. Te cobran hasta por los permisos para aplanar el terreno. Encima que pagas al palista, te cobra el ayuntamiento. Todo son problemas”. Una mujer llora sentada sobre sus cosas después de vaciar su casa por la amenaza del volcán de La Palma. La pérdida del hogar Es difícil sentir un hogar allí donde es difícil construir un proyecto de vida. La incertidumbre ha inundado las vidas de sus vecinos, y preguntas como “¿hasta cuando podré quedarme en el contenedor?”, o “¿cuándo podré empezar reconstruir mi casa?” se arremolinan en la mente de los vecinos. “Vecinos que nacieron ahí, se criaron ahí, y de pronto toda tu raíz… ¿qué pasa con toda esa parte que desaparece y no queda rastro?”, relata Belqui, cuya casa en el barrio de Tajuya se salvó por muy poco. El volcán se ha llevado, en tan sólo 85 días, lo que para muchos vecinos es el esfuerzo de 30 años de trabajo. Y les ha quitado, además del esfuerzo, y en contraposición, el descanso. Porque un hogar también es poder llegar a casa y tumbarse en el sofá, sabiendo que nadie ni nada interrumpirá ese momento. Durante cinco años, los vecinos damnificados han pasado por muchas ubicaciones, pero ninguna a largo plazo, y ninguna donde poder descansar plenamente. Habitaciones en albergues, contenedores, casas de familiares o alquileres temporales han compuesto algunas de las soluciones aportadas a los vecinos. Pero llevando siempre una maleta a cuestas, es difícil construir un hogar.
